Paramount's Star Trek reboot drops Kirk for new era

Paramount's Star Trek reboot drops Kirk for new era

Kirk era ends: Paramount's next Star Trek film will not feature Captain Kirk or other original series characters, instead introducing a new crew set in a later period of the franchise timeline.

The studio confirmed the reboot will move away from the Kelvin-timeline cast that headlined the 2009 relaunch and its two sequels, ending a run that began seventeen years ago and never produced a fourth instalment despite repeated announcements.

Producers described the decision as a generational reset intended to let new audiences enter the franchise without needing to know the earlier films, while long-running characters are retired rather than recast.

Fetterman abandons his 2022 filibuster pledge

John Fetterman has reversed his position on the Senate filibuster: the Pennsylvania Democrat now supports keeping it after he previously campaigned to eliminate it in 2022, and he says Democrats were horribly wrong to push the other way when they briefly held the majority.

What the filibuster actually does

The shift matters because Fetterman is not only revising an old campaign promise but doing so while his party debates whether the rule protects them in the minority, reviving a fight Democrats have never fully settled.

Fetterman laid out his new position in a July 28 column, arguing that the rule blocked action when his party held power but now shields whichever side is out of power from the other's most sweeping legislation.

Mortgage rates edged lower for a third consecutive week, offering modest relief to buyers who have spent the year contending with the highest borrowing costs in more than two decades and a persistent shortage of listings.

Economists cautioned that the decline is unlikely to change affordability materially until inventory improves in the larger metropolitan markets.
